subject: Operational Readiness Snapshot — July outage recap & QBR talking points
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption this morning — brief recap

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround this morning. Our payments flow experienced elevated latencies between ~02:12-02:38 PDT (approx 26 minutes). We saw 18% of checkout requests hit the 2s+ tail and a small set of timeouts triggered automatic retry logic in our client which caused duplicate charges for two customers (we're handling refunds).

I attached our outbound error logs and a short timeline. Primary ask: we need a concise one-page summary and an action list that we can share with our procurement and legal folks ahead of our upcoming QBR on Tuesday.

Appreciate the partnership.

—John
John Doe
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Corp

Attachments: acme-outbound-errors-20270715.ndjson (attachment stub), acme-timeline.csv (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Operational Readiness Snapshot — July outage recap & QBR talking points

John — thanks for the timeline and signals. High-level recap below (we'll turn this into the one-pager for Acme and the internal QBR slide).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: memory pressure on a small subset of dedicated inference workers during a spike of long-context batch requests; GC churn amplified latency.
- Impact window: 02:12–02:38 PDT; 18% of checkout requests saw >2s latencies; 2 confirmed duplicate charges (client retry), no data exfiltration.
- Immediate mitigations enacted: isolated affected pool, rolled a hotfix that reduces KV cache memory growth, and enabled short-circuit failover to a lower-capacity variant for premium customers.

Action owners (first pass):
- Hotfix review + permanent mitigation: Rishi Malhotra (VP Eng) — due 2027-07-20
- Production monitoring rule & runbook updates: Hannah Schmitt (SRE Lead) — due 2027-07-18
- Customer-facing one-pager + compensation recommendation: Marissa Cole (Head of Reliability) — due 2027-07-17
- Legal/procurement coordination (Acme contract lead): Vivek Kulkarni (CTO) — assist as needed

I'm attaching a draft incident timeline and an initial QBR slide deck. Feedback welcome; I'll circulate a final deck by EOD Monday so leadership has time to review before Tuesday's QBR.

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-timeline-20270715.pdf (attachment stub), qbr-slides-draft-v1.pptx (attachment stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational Readiness Snapshot — July outage recap & QBR talking points

Marissa — good summary. Quick clarifications and commitments from eng: 

Notes:
- The memory pressure was triggered by a recent change in batching heuristics for long-context (>8k) sessions. That heuristic increased prefix caching aggressiveness; we missed a corner where escaping KV entries for some sharded models weren't freed promptly.
- Hotfix we pushed this morning is a GC guard for the cache and reduces the aggressiveness of that heuristic for the affected model family. Early telemetry looks clean.

Committed follow-ups (owners + timeline):
1) Root cause write-up + permanent fix plan (including test cases): Rishi — 2027-07-20
2) Backfill unit/integration tests for cache lifecycle: Eng infra team (owner: Priya Natarajan) — 2027-07-27
3) Rollout policy change to enable canary guardrails for heuristic changes: Rishi & Hannah — 2027-07-30

I'll attach the minimal repro snippet to the RCA.

On customer communication: Marissa, I agree with your one-pager approach. From an engineering perspective, recommend we offer a 1-week credit tied to token usage during impact window rather than wholesale SLA write-offs; keeps it pragmatic for procurement.

—Rishi
VP, Engineering

Team — quick executive priorities:

1) Customer first: finalize the one-pager and compensation recommendation (Marissa) by EOD tomorrow. We need a clear statement of impact, steps we took, and proposed remedy.
2) Risk to QBR narrative: the deck should show root cause and plan; do not over-index on internal detail — keep the slide to 3 bullets + timeline + ask. Hannah, add a single slide showing "what we're changing" and the expected date of resolution.
3) Internal ops: Rishi, prioritize automated alerts for cache growth; this is recurring risk across model families.

If Acme pushes on SLA credits publicly or with procurement, we should have the math ready (cost of outage vs precedent). Rishi's credit recommendation makes sense as a starting point.

Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference

Monitoring and runbooks:
- Temporary: we enabled a short window alert (cache-resident-entries > 85% capacity for > 3min) and an automated pool isolation play. These are in effect now.
- Permanent: update runbook to include explicit steps for forced evictions and safe-failover to variant pools. Owner: Hannah — due 2027-07-18.

QBR slide content (3 bullets + timeline):
1) Impact summary + customer scope (brief)
2) Root cause + mitigations (what we changed immediately)
3) Next steps & expected completion dates (owners and dates)
